sections.advice: Red Lodge → Top of the World is 34 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Top of the World → Beartooth Pass climbs about 3337 m in 3 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Beartooth Pass → Cooke City drops about 3337 m over 46 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.
Cooke City → Yellowstone Northeast Entrance is 7 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.

scenicChapters.title: Beartooth Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: For 47 km this is Beartooth Highway, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Beartooth Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it. The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 3337 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Beartooth Pass → Cooke City
scenicChapters.narrative: 3337 m come off over 64 km at around 7.2%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it — brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

beartooth-highway.story: A 126 km one-way ride from near Red Lodge, about 2 h 03 of riding. The stops in between: Top of the World, Beartooth Pass and Cooke City. The highest point is about 3,350 m. Beartooth Pass is open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. It suits an unhurried touring pace.
